purpose: Independent practice of A6.9 — sharing a small group equally onto plates and reasoning about leftovers.
student_learning_goal: I can share a small group of things equally onto plates so each plate has the same amount.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can share a small group of things equally onto plates so each plate has the same amount.
header.character_watermark: Penny the Lead Coin Counter in the top-right corner of the header, sharing cookies onto plates. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Look at each scene. Share the things equally between the plates. Draw the share. Then write how many on each plate.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Three sharing scenes stacked vertically. Scene A: 8 cookies in a tray on the left, 2 empty plates on the right. Scene B: 12 grapes in a bowl on the left, 3 empty plates on the right. Scene C: 9 stickers in a sheet on the left, 3 empty plates on the right. Each scene has a blank line under each plate for the count.

image_placeholders.description: Three sharing scenes stacked vertically in B&W line-art, each ~2in tall. Scene A: a tray with 8 round cookies on the left, 2 paper plates with light-grey outlines on the right. Scene B: a bowl with 12 round grapes on the left, 3 paper plates on the right. Scene C: a sticker sheet with 9 stars on the left, 3 paper plates on the right. Each plate is ~1.5in diameter.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; three scenes spanning the page width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_THREE_SHARE_SCENES at top: keywords (cookies, grapes, stickers, plates, share) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 4 cookies on each plate. Scene B: 4 grapes on each plate. Scene C: 3 stickers on each plate.

parts.student_instructions: Some shares don't come out even. Share fairly. Circle the LEFTOVER. Then write what you would do with it.
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two leftover scenes stacked. Scene A: 7 cookies on the left, 2 plates on the right. Scene B: 10 grapes on the left, 3 plates on the right. Below each scene: a small red circle to draw around the leftover, plus a thought-bubble line for the child's leftover plan.

image_placeholders.description: Two leftover scenes stacked in B&W line-art. Scene A: 7 round cookies on the left, 2 paper plates on the right. Scene B: 10 round grapes on the left, 3 paper plates on the right. Each scene has a small red-circle outline for the leftover indicator and a thought-bubble below for the leftover plan.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; two scenes spanning full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_TWO_LEFTOVER_SCENES at middle: keywords (cookies, grapes, leftover, plates) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 3 cookies on each plate, 1 leftover. Scene B: 3 grapes on each plate, 1 leftover. Leftover plans accepted: 'cut in half', 'give to teacher', 'eat together', 'save for later', 'put in jar'. Any plausible plan that the child can articulate.

parts.student_instructions: Draw your own sharing scene. Pick what you are sharing (cookies, grapes, or anything else!) and how many friends. Use the sentence starter.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box (~5in × 3in) with a light-grey outline for the child's drawing. Below the box, a sentence starter line: 'I shared ___ between ___ friends. Each friend got ___.'

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing frame in B&W line-art, ~5in × 3in, with a light-grey solid outline. Decorative paper plates icon (~0.5in) sits in each corner of the frame. Below the frame, a faint dotted line for the sentence starter.
image_placeholders.placement: Bottom of the page; spans full width.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_BLANK_SHARING_FRAME at bottom: keywords (sharing, plates, friends) name what the frame shows.

parts.answer_key: Any valid sharing scene where (a) the total objects can be evenly or near-evenly divided, (b) the sentence starter is filled in correctly. Examples: 'I shared 6 cookies between 2 friends. Each friend got 3.' 'I shared 9 grapes between 3 friends. Each friend got 3.' Accept leftover scenarios as well.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and try sharing 11 things between 4 friends. What happens to the leftover?
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation. Hand out after the small-group sharing rounds. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 with minimal prompting if the dealing strategy was solid in the lesson. Watch for: (a) a child who SCOOPS in Part 1 instead of dealing — the worksheet result may be right but the strategy is fragile (refer back to lesson 4 expanded_walkthrough); (b) a child who can't articulate a leftover plan in Part 2 — flag for re-loop on the leftover concept. Part 3 captures whether the child has internalised fair-share as a model.
